title: Imputing Incomplete ISO 8601 Dates with ks_impute_dtc()
text: ISO 8601 dates clinical data sources often truncated: patient visit recorded "2020-03" means “sometime March 2020”, value "2020" means “sometime 2020”. title: Multiple Imputation Analysis with mianalyze()
text: Missing data common clinical trials, observational studies, registries, real-world evidence analyses. standard approach handling missing values multiple imputation (MI), several complete datasets generated, containing plausible replacements missing observations. analysing imputed dataset, analyst obtains: parameter estimate imputation; corresponding standard error. final step combine results single inference. process commonly known pooling MI analysis described Rubin (1987). mianalyze() function kstools implements Rubin’s pooling rules supports Barnard-Rubin (1999) small-sample degrees--freedom adjustment, equivalent EDF= option SAS PROC MIANALYZE. exported alias ks_mianalyze() provides interface.

title: Area Under the Curve (AUC) by the trapezoidal rule — ks_auc
text: Linear trapezoid (type = "trapez"): $$AUC_i = \frac{C_i + C_{+1}}{2} \cdot (t_{+1} - t_i)$$ Log-linear trapezoid (type = "log-trapez"): $$AUC_i = \frac{C_{+1} - C_i}{\ln C_{+1} - \ln C_i} \cdot (t_{+1} - t_i)$$ log-linear method preferred elimination phases concentrations decline exponentially.  requires strictly positive concentrations; two consecutive values equal one \(\leq 0\) interval automatically falls back linear rule. Rows sorted c(, time) computing caller need pre-sort data.

title: Area Under the Curve (AUC) by the trapezoidal rule — ks_auc
code: ## Single subject — linear trapezoid pk1 <- data.frame(conc = c(0, 4, 2, 1), time = c(0, 1, 2, 4)) ks_auc(pk1, val = conc, time = time) #> [1] 8  ## Two subjects — grouped pk2 <- data.frame(   id   = c("A","A","A","B","B","B"),   conc = c(0, 4, 1,  0, 6, 2),   time = c(0, 1, 2,  0, 1, 2) ) ks_auc(pk2, by = "id", val = conc, time = time) #>   id AUC #> 1  A 4.5 #> 2  B 7.0

title: Analogue of SAS PROC MIANALYZE (Rubin pooling) — ks_mianalyze
text: Let \(Q_i\) \(U_i\) estimate variance imputation \(\). pooled estimate \(\bar{Q} = m^{-1}\sum_i Q_i\); within variance \(\bar{U} = m^{-1}\sum_i U_i\); variance \(B = (m-1)^{-1}\sum_i (Q_i-\bar{Q})^2\); total variance \(T = \bar{U} + (1 + 1/m)B\). Rubin's (1987) large-sample degrees freedom \(v_m = (m-1)(1 + \bar{U}/((1+m^{-1})B))^2\).  complete-data degrees freedom \(v_0\) small fraction missing information modest, \(v_m\) can greatly exceed \(v_0\), inappropriate.  Barnard-Rubin (1999) adjustment computes \(v_m^* = (1/v_m + 1/\hat{v}_{obs})^{-1}\) \(\hat{v}_{obs} = (1-\gamma) v_0 (v_0+1)/(v_0+3)\) \(\gamma = (1+m^{-1})B/T\). within-imputation variance \(\bar{U}\) exactly zero, df, r, lambda, re, confidence limits \(t\)-test reported NA warning issued. mirrors PROC MIANALYZE, warns per zero standard error prints "." quantities, computing inference case - without EDF= - even -imputation variance positive. Validated live SAS PROC MIANALYZE run; probe tooling deliberately kept outside package.

title: Newcombe Hybrid Score CI for a difference of two proportions — ks_newcombe_hs
text: Algorithm (Newcombe, 1998): Compute Wilson score CI \([l_i,\, u_i]\) group     level \(1-\alpha\):     $$l_i,\, u_i = \frac{2x_i + z^2 \mp z\sqrt{z^2 + 4x_i(n_i-x_i)/n_i}}{2(n_i + z^2)}$$ Form CI \(\delta = p_1 - p_2\):     $$\mathrm{LCL} = \hat\delta - \sqrt{(p_1-l_1)^2 + (u_2-p_2)^2}$$     $$\mathrm{UCL} = \hat\delta + \sqrt{(u_1-p_1)^2 + (p_2-l_2)^2}$$ function vectorised: vectors length \(k\) supplied, corresponding tuple \((x_{1i}, n_{1i}, x_{2i}, n_{2i})\) processed independently result \(k \times 3\) matrix.

title: Stratified Newcombe Hybrid Score CI for a difference of two proportions — ks_newcombe_hs_strata
text: Algorithm: Compute Wilson CIs \([l_{1i},\,u_{1i}]\)     \([l_{2i},\,u_{2i}]\) stratum \(\). Assign stratum weights     \(W_i = n_{1i}\,n_{2i} / (n_{1i} + n_{2i})\)     (harmonic-mean / Mantel-Haenszel weights). Pooled point estimate:     \(\hat\delta = \sum W_i (p_{1i}-p_{2i}) / \sum W_i\). Pooled lower limit:     $$\mathrm{LCL} = \hat\delta -       \sqrt{\frac{\sum W_i^2(p_{1i}-l_{1i})^2}{(\sum W_i)^2} +             \frac{\sum W_i^2(u_{2i}-p_{2i})^2}{(\sum W_i)^2}}$$ Pooled upper limit: analogously. single stratum reduces un-stratified formula.
